title: Nuisance Bleed Overheat Warnings in the Descent — Request for a Sensing Installation Review
abstract: Baltic Crown Airlines reports repeated bleed overheat warnings in the descent that clear on the ground and cannot be reproduced, and asks whether the sensing installation near the pylon firewall is the cause.

sections.request: Our crews are getting a bleed overheat caution during descent, mostly on the right engine, and by the time the aircraft is on stand the message has gone and the maintenance system shows nothing meaningful. We have swapped the obvious boxes twice on two aircraft and it made no difference. Every one of these events costs us a delay, because the crew are quite right to run the procedure and we then have to do a ground run before the next sector. It only happens on cold, wet days and it does not happen in the climb. Our engineers think the sensing element is picking up something local rather than a real duct temperature, and they have asked us to put the question to you formally rather than keep changing parts.
sections.background: Nine events across six aircraft since last October, all on descent, all in northern European winter conditions. Two engine bleed system components were replaced with no change in behaviour. We have no evidence of any actual duct overtemperature: borescope of the affected ducting was clean and there is no thermal discolouration. Dispatch reliability on the affected group has dropped by about half a point since the events started.
sections.expected_outcome: Either a confirmation that the current sensing installation is correct and a troubleshooting route that actually converges, or a change to where and how the sensing elements are held so that the warning stops appearing when there is no overheat.

type_data.business_justification: Nine delay events in one winter season, each costing a ground run and an average of fifty-five minutes of schedule, with two unnecessary component replacements already charged to the operator.
